newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Woolworths sees subdued conditions.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Woolworths sees subdued conditions.

text.p: Australian grocery retailer Woolworths Ltd said on Thursday that trading conditions would remain subdued in the current financial year ending June 30, 1997 but it would continue with its store expansion policy.

"Notwithstanding the subdued trading environment, the rate of expansion will continue during the current year, taking advantage of those areas throughout Australia which we perceive will have continuing growth potential," chairman John Iliffe said in the 1995/96 annual report.

The report did not contain any revision to 1996/97 sales or profit forecasts. The supermarkets and specialty stores group said on August 21 when it released the 1995/96 accounts that it expected earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) to grow this financial year after ebit rose by 6.8 percent in 1995/96.

Woolworths managing director and chief executive Reg Clairs said in the report that while 1995/96 was one of the toughest for retailers in recent memory, the company had still be able to achieve a 9.35 percent rise in sales to A$13.99 million.
Clairs said the company planned to have 500 supermarkets in operation by the year 2000 and 100 Big W stores.

"Eighteen Woolworths developments are scheduled for completion by June 1997," he said. "These will account for approximately half of all new major supermarkets due to open in Australia during the year ended June 1997."
"Big W's new store programme has also made impressive progress, with eight stores opened during the year, and a similar number expected to be completed by June 1997," he said.
Woolworths's 1995/96 (July-June) pre-tax operating profit rose 5.56 percent to A$360.6 million, while net profit steady at A$233.6 million due to a higher tax rate.
